label: Claude Haiku 5.5
output:
Hello Tolu, I'm Amaka. I'm in 100L Biology now and I wanted Medicine too, so I know exactly how you're feeling. I cried for a whole day when I saw it. I locked myself in my cousin's room in Surulere and didn't eat. So I'm not going to tell you it's nothing. But I'll be straight with you about what I know, what I don't, and what I'd check if I were you.

**My own story first**

I scored 251 in JAMB 2025 and applied for Medicine and Surgery. I got Biology at a federal university here in Lagos. For about two months I didn't tell people anything, and my mum was telling everybody at church that I was doing Medicine. I had to beg her to stop. That part was hard in its own way.

Then first-year Biology started, and something happened that I didn't expect. In our first practical we dissected toads. One guy in my group fainted. I was fine, and that day I realised I actually like this thing. I'm enjoying genetics and cell biology more than I thought I would. I'm not saying that to make you feel better. It's just what happened to me.

**The real transfer situation**

This is the part I want you to hear clearly, because people online give very different answers.

Transfer to Medicine is possible, but it is NOT easy, and nobody should accept Biology thinking it's automatic. Our level adviser told us the requirements. You need a CGPA of at least 4.5 out of 5, and there must be space in the MBBS programme. Space is the big one. Last year, about 6 people got moved in from the whole faculty, and she thinks over 40 people applied. So the numbers are very tight.

My CGPA after first semester is 4.31. That's not 4.5, so I'm not there yet. I'm still trying. I'm telling you this so you know I'm not writing from a place of "I made it, so you can too." I'm still in the middle of it.

Also, the adviser said that to be considered for transfer you need the Medicine cut-off in JAMB and the post-UTME cut-off too. I don't know your school's cut-offs or your post-UTME score, so please check both. Your 268 alone doesn't tell you whether you're eligible. Don't assume.

**What 100L is actually like**

The courses in 100L are BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101, and GST. Physics and maths are the ones that deal with people. Maths especially. Don't underestimate them just because it's "Biology." Start reading early and don't wait for the exam season to panic.

Also budget for the extras, because nobody warns you about this. My lab coat was 6,500 naira, the dissecting kit was 9k, and the practical manual was extra on top. Those costs add up, so plan for them before the semester starts.

**Is Biology bad?**

No. It's not a bad course. It's a real science, and it has its own hard parts, but it isn't a consolation prize. If you go in with the attitude that you're just waiting to leave, you'll have a miserable time and probably do worse. If you go in and actually engage with it, you might find something you like. That's what happened to me, but it may not happen to you, and that's okay too.

**On rewriting and staying home**

I won't tell you rewriting is wrong. If you're ready to rewrite, sit for JAMB again, and you have a real plan for it, that's a valid choice. I have a classmate from secondary school, Ifeoma, who rejected a Pharmacy offer to rewrite for Medicine. She has written JAMB two more times and she's still at home. I'm not saying that to scare you. I'm saying it because staying home is not as easy as people make it sound. You'll watch your mates go to school, and that can really get to you. Both paths have a cost. Don't pick one just because someone online says it's easy.

**Some things to ask yourself**

Before you decide, I'd ask yourself: do I want Medicine, or do I want to be a doctor for my parents? Those can be two different things. If it's the second, that's worth knowing before you make a big choice.

Also, go to your faculty or department and ask the exact transfer rules for your own school. Ask what the CGPA requirement is, how many spaces there are for transfer, and when the process happens. Don't just trust forum people, including me. Rules differ between schools, and I only know my own school's situation.

**My honest advice**

Check your acceptance deadline right now. You said it's two weeks from the 6th, so don't leave it until the last day. Find out your school's Medicine cut-offs and your post-UTME score. Go and talk to the faculty. Then decide whether you're choosing Biology as a step toward Medicine, choosing Biology because you like it, or choosing to rewrite because you're ready for that year. Any of those is a legitimate choice.

Whatever you choose, it is not the end of the world. I know it feels like it right now. You're 19. There are a lot of years ahead, and a lot of routes to end up where you want to be. Take care of yourself, eat something, and please talk to someone you trust offline too.

If you have questions about 100L or the practicals, ask me here. I'll answer honestly.
